newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Bruton upbeat on EMU prospects.
newsitem.headline: Bruton upbeat on EMU prospects.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Friday that the fact EU states had reached agreement on an EMU stability pact ahead of time showed strong political will across the bloc for Economic and Monetary Union.
"That shows there is the political will to make this project work," said Bruton, nearing the end of the six-month Irish EU presidency.

He was speaking hours after the two-dau EU summit clinched an agreement on the terms of a stability pact to underpin the EMU project after marathon overnight discussions by EU finance ministers ended without agreement.
Bruton said the summit would issue a Dublin Declaration to cut the EU's jobless queues, which currently total 18.5 million people.
The statement will call for greater coordination of training and employment policies but steer clear of putting targets on the number of jobs the EU wants to create, EU diplomats said.
Bruton said he differed with British Prime Minister John Major who told an earlier news conference, "A declaration of this sort will not create a single job."
Bruton said the declaration, to be made public on Saturday, would call for greater adaptability and training among member states to attack unemployment and would not undermine national efforts.
"The level of employment in the European Union in 10 years' time will be determined by how adaptable the EU is to change in the world," he said.
Bruton said the EU faced stiff competition from East Asian and Pacific rim states who had shown greater capacity to change and the EU had lessons to learn.
"By putting the emphasis on change and training, the Declaration will create a climate that facilitates EU adaptability," he said.
